name: Lake Waikaremoana Great Walk
why: Four days around a forest lake in Te Urewera, the homeland of Ngāi Tūhoe: first a ridge walk along the Panekire Bluff high above the water, then bays, beaches and falls along the shore.
book: Huts and campsites must be booked all year (fees per night). The two ends are about 30 km apart by road: book the Tūhoe water taxi (usually Oct-Apr) or a shuttle from Te Urewera Visitor Centre at Te Kura Whenua. SH38 is gravel for about 90 km.
water: Hut tap water is untreated: boil, filter or treat it. Panekire Hut tank water can run low in summer.
dangers: About 600 m of steep climb and descent over the Panekire Range, exposed to wind and cloud.
Cold, snow, strong wind and heavy rain can come at any time of year; the rainforest tracks get muddy.
Huts have no gas cookers, lighting or toilet paper: carry a stove and fuel.
turnaround: Plan the Panekire Range for a clear day: if it is in cloud and wind, wait at Onepoto or the hut rather than walk the ridge blind.

points.name: Onepoto
points.note: Start at the Onepoto shelter on SH38, through the site of the old Armed Constabulary redoubt.

points.name: Panekiri Bluff
points.note: The track tops the bluff and follows the cliff edge, the lake and its arms far below.

points.name: Panekire Hut
points.note: First night, 36 bunks on the range past Puketapu Trig (1,180 m), 8.8 km and 4-6 hours from Onepoto.

points.name: Waiopaoa Hut
points.note: Second night at the mouth of the Waiopaoa inlet, after a steep drop off the range. Korokoro Falls is a 1 hour side trip further on.

points.name: Marauiti Hut
points.note: Third night over Whakaneke Ridge; at dusk you may hear kiwi on the Puketukutuku Peninsula.

points.name: Hopuruahine Landing
points.note: The northern end, over the Hopuruahine suspension bridge. Water taxi pick-up; the road car park is 2 km away.
